title: AI trader architecture: one generalist model over all markets vs one specialist per market (BTC, ETH, S&P...), kept side by side and continuously compared; plus a committee (consensus vote / best-reasoning judge / shared-reasoning deliberation)
note: OPERATOR 2026-10-27 ~07:20Z (chat, close paraphrase): the main AI goal is still ONE overarching in-house AI that watches markets and manages trades from start to end. Keep BOTH shapes and always test which is better: (a) one overall model for all markets (sees everything, cross-market context), (b) one model per traded market (BTC, ETH, S&P 500 ...; attuned to that market). Possibly best is both, with several models taking part in every decision as a COMMITTEE: choose by consensus/most agreement, or by best reasoning if each model can state its reasoning and that can be judged, or by models sharing reasoning and deciding together. 'A level of design we are definitely not at yet' -- keep in mind as the ML side is built; discuss and possibly test NEXT WEEK. Scope for the week-of-2026-11-02 plan: a design note + pre-registered research units comparing generalist vs per-market students on the DESK-19 handoff data (same labels, OOS net R per capital-day), and a committee arm; feeds DESK-19 / ml-plan-items.yaml / the Sunday /ml-review step 9 ML plan loop.
